question: A shopkeeper marks his goods at X% above the cost price and sells them at a discount of 35%. If he makes a profit of 69%, find the value of X.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Direct formula for ratio of Marked Price (MP) to Cost Price (CP):

MP ÷ CP = (100 + Profit%) ÷ (100 − Discount%)

MP ÷ CP = (100 + 69) ÷ (100 − 35) = 169 ÷ 65 = 13 ÷ 5

Markup amount = 13 − 5 = 8 parts over a base CP of 5 parts.

Markup % = (8 ÷ 5) × 100 = 160%

**∴ The correct answer is 160.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Profit percentage = 69%

Discount percentage = 35%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100

Selling Price (SP) = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100

 CP SP MP 
 
 Markup = X% 
 
 −35% (Discount) 
 
 +69% (Profit) 

**Calculations:**

Let the Cost Price (CP) be 100.

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = 100 × (100 + 69) ÷ 100 = 169

⇒ SP is also determined by applying a 35% discount on Marked Price (MP).

⇒ 169 = MP × (100 − 35) ÷ 100

⇒ 169 = MP × 65 ÷ 100

⇒ MP = 169 × 100 ÷ 65

⇒ MP = 13 × 100 ÷ 5 = 260

⇒ Markup amount = MP − CP = 260 − 100 = 160

⇒ Markup % (X) = (160 ÷ 100) × 100 = 160%

**∴ The correct answer is 160.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Cost Price Relation

The direct relation between MP and CP is given by: MP ÷ CP = (100 + P%) ÷ (100 − D%).

Successive Discount

For two successive discounts D₁% and D₂%, the equivalent single discount is given by (D₁ + D₂ − D₁×D₂ ÷ 100)%.

Dishonest Dealer Concept

When a seller uses false weights and sells at CP, Profit% = [(True Weight − False Weight) ÷ False Weight] × 100.
